person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: A model based on n-ary relations, a normal form for data base relations, and the concept of a universal data sublanguage are introduced.

span.label: data independence in shared data banks
span.quote: In contrast, the problems treated here are those of data independence--the independence of application programs and terminal activities from growth in data types and changes in data representation--and certain kinds of data inconsistency which are expected to become troublesome even in nondeductive systems.

span.label: formal-theory
span.quote: Implementations of systems to support the relational model are not discussed.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: represent data as mathematical relations (tables) decoupled from physical storage, so programs are independent of how data is stored and can be queried with a high-level relational language
span.quote: a high level data language which will yield maximal independence

span.label: the range of representation changes achievable without impairing programs is still limited
span.note: what this limits: the data-independence claim: the range of representation changes THAT CAN BE CHANGED WITHOUT LOGICALLY IMPAIRING SOME APPLICATION PROGRAMS IS STILL QUITE LIMITED
span.quote: which can be changed without logically impairing some application programs is still quite limited

span.label: The paper deliberately excludes any discussion of how systems supporting the model would be implemented.
span.note: what this limits: any implementation reading: IMPLEMENTATIONS OF SYSTEMS TO SUPPORT THE RELATIONAL MODEL ARE NOT DISCUSSED
span.quote: Implementations of systems to support the relational model are not discussed.

span.label: Further normalisation operations exist but are left out of the paper.
span.note: what this limits: the normalisation account as complete: further operations exist and THESE ARE NOT DISCUSSED IN THIS PAPER
span.quote: These are not discussed in this paper.

span.label: The proposed data sublanguage is only sketched; neither its linguistic detail nor its implementation is worked out.
span.note: what this limits: any use of the paper as a specification for a query language: NEITHER THE PURELY LINGUISTIC DETAILS OF SUCH A LANGUAGE NOR THE IMPLEMENTATION PROBLEMS ARE DISCUSSED
span.quote: Neither the purely linguistic details of such a language nor the implementation problems are discussed.

span.label: Checking consistency requires an instantaneous snapshot of possibly very large, highly variable relations, a practical problem the paper does not address.
span.note: what this limits: the consistency-checking proposal at scale: THERE ARE PRACTICAL PROBLEMS (WHICH WE SHALL NOT DISCUSS HERE) IN TAKING AN INSTANTANEOUS SNAPSHOT OF A COLLECTION OF RELATIONS, SOME OF WHICH MAY BE VERY LARGE AND HIGHLY VARIABLE
span.quote: There are practical problems (which we shall not discuss here) in taking an instantaneous snapshot of a collection of relations, some of which may be very large and highly variable.

span.label: Following a chain of stored connections to answer a question is stated to be erroneous in general; it is valid only when the target relation IS the natural composition of the links, and only if that holds for all time.
span.note: what this limits: any answer obtained by following paths through linked records: it is correct only in the very special case that the target relation is the natural composition of the relations traversed, and the phrase 'for all time' must normally be added
span.quote: Such a conclusion is correct only in the very special case that the target relation between projects and suppliers is, in fact, the natural composition of the other two relations--and we must normally add the phrase "for all time," because this is usually implied in claims concerning path-following techniques

span.label: The normalisation procedure is stated to apply only when the collection of relations already satisfies stated structural conditions.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that a collection of relations can be normalised: the procedure requires the graph of interrelationships of the nonsimple domains to be a collection of trees
span.quote: If normalization as described above is to be applicable, the unnormalized collection of relations must satisfy the following conditions: (1) The graph of interrelationships of the nonsimple domains is a collection of trees

span.label: A distinction the paper draws is then declared not worth maintaining for the rest of the paper.
span.note: what this limits: the words 'relation' and 'relationship' anywhere after Section 1: the paper states it will not distinguish them except where being explicit is advantageous
span.quote: In the remainder of this paper, we shall not bother to distinguish between relations and relationships except where it appears advantageous to be explicit

span.label: modelling data as mathematical n-ary relations queried via predicate calculus, giving data independence
span.quote: A model based on n-ary relations, a normal form for data base relations, and the concept of a universal data sublanguage are introduced

span.label: relational model
span.quote: The relational view (or model) of data described in Section 1 appears to be superior in several respects to the graph or network model

span.label: normalization
span.quote: There is, in fact, a very simple elimination procedure, which we shall call normalization

span.label: data independence
span.quote: the problems treated here are those of data independence--the independence of application programs and terminal activities from growth in data types and changes in data representation

span.label: connection trap
span.quote: A lack of understanding of relational composition has led several systems designers into what may be called the connection trap

span.label: foreign key
span.quote: We shall call a domain (or domain combination) of relation R a foreign key if it is not the primary key of R but its elements are values of the primary key of some relation

span.label: primary key
span.quote: The primary key of each relation is italicized to show how such keys are expanded by the normalization

span.label: the connection trap - A NAMED ERROR: mistaking the derivation of connections for the derivation of relations, which the paper attributes to a lack of understanding of relational composition
span.quote: A lack of understanding of relational composition has led several systems designers into what may be called the connection trap

span.label: derivability - HOLDING FOR ALL TIME, not at an instant: because the relations vary in time, the sequence of operations must yield the relation over a significant period, not once
span.quote: The phrase "for all time" is present, because we are dealing with time-varying relations, and our interest is in derivability which holds over a significant period of time

span.label: data independence - AS INDEPENDENCE FROM TWO THINGS AT ONCE: growth in data types, and changes in data representation, for application programs and terminal activities alike
span.quote: the problems treated here are those of data independence--the independence of application programs and terminal activities from growth in data types and changes in data representation
